name: Review Rough Cut
description: Quality gate that validates the assembled rough cut for duration consistency, narrative coherence, and complete thoughts before proceeding to planning phases. Rejects manifests with mismatched source/timeline durations or incoherent narrative flow.

inputs.name: render_qa_findings
inputs.description: The LAST render's QA findings, read off exports/qa_report.json by library/tools/qa_findings.py. No DAG edge carries it: the producer is step 6.02, the final node, so an edge here would be a back edge and the topological sort would refuse it. It is filled by name in gather_step_inputs for the steps that declare it, and it is absent on a project that has never rendered. It carries its own legend, because handoff.md is frozen. NOT a gate: an advisory finding must never reject a rough cut.

inputs.name: temporal_index
inputs.description: State input: temporal_index - the word-level index step 1.04 wrote, mapped from its `temporal_event_indices`. It is the only input this step is routed that is a MEASUREMENT rather than an upstream decision, and it is what Check 5 - which this handoff calls the most important step of Part 2 - reconstructs the actual script from. It reaches the prompt through `view:transcript`, which leaves the per-word timings behind (AGENTS.md 10.1); step.py still receives the whole thing unprojected.

inputs.name: timeline_notes
inputs.description: The captain's own notes typed onto the built timeline in DaVinci Resolve, routed to this step because this step owns the decision each note is about. Injected by the runner from <project>/marker_feedback/ and absent when there are none. See library/tools/marker_routing.py.

outputs.name: roughcut_window_frames
outputs.description: A map of the frame strips the deterministic half drew, one per PLACED window - every A-roll segment and every B-roll overlay the cut plays, in timeline order - with the directory holding them. Prompt-only: it shows the review what the cut LOOKS like beside the prose that says what it does. See library/tools/window_frames.build_review_block. Absent on a run that drew none, and the review then judges from the prose alone.

outputs.name: cut_decisions
outputs.description: The narrative half of this step: one record per CUT, judging how the cut reads. Shape: [{"cut_point_position": <the position of the spine block the cut leads INTO, as it appears in audio_spine.structure>, "verdict": "smooth"|"acceptable"|"jarring"|"broken", "why": "one sentence"}]. The four words are Check 7's own vocabulary in this handoff; this declaration states the SHAPE the schema injector asks for and adds no criterion the handoff does not already carry. Judge a cut only where you have something to say - a cut you name no verdict for reads as UNJUDGED downstream, which is not the verdict 'smooth'. Read by step 4.02 plan_transitions, which folds it onto its cuts table as `narrative_verdict` and `verdict_note`; see library/tools/cut_verdicts.py.

llm_outputs.name: cut_decisions
llm_outputs.description: One record per CUT the model judges, in the shape the cut_decisions output declares. Judge a cut only where you have something to say.

llm_outputs.name: rough_cut_review
llm_outputs.description: The narrative review: the reconstructed script, sentence completion, narrative flow, emotional arc, key moments, and note_acknowledgements for any timeline_notes.
